title: DJI Avata 2 live stream with Goggles 3: Instagram, TikTok, YouTube
description: How to live stream FPV footage from a DJI Avata 2: share the Goggles 3 view to DJI Fly on your phone, stream over RTMP and go live on Instagram, TikTok or YouTube.
h1: How to live stream a DJI Avata 2
lead: The Avata 2 has no screen controller, so the stream leaves through your phone: Goggles 3 share their live view with DJI Fly, and DJI Fly sends it over RTMP. Point that at DJI Live Bridge on a computer and the FPV picture goes on to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube or several platforms at once.
summary: Connect DJI Goggles 3 to your phone — a USB-C cable is the most reliable — and open DJI Fly to see the live view.
In DJI Fly: GO FLY → ••• → Transmission → Live Streaming Platforms → RTMP, with the address DJI Live Bridge shows.
The phone's Wi-Fi must be on the same network as the computer; the cable keeps it free for that.
DJI Live Bridge reshapes the landscape FPV picture into vertical 1080×1920 for Instagram and TikTok.
A spotter or a second person should handle the stream — the pilot is wearing goggles.

sections.h2: How streaming works with an FPV drone

blocks.p: With the Avata 2 the picture goes from the drone to the goggles. DJI Goggles 3 can share that live view with DJI Fly on a phone, by cable or over Wi-Fi, and DJI Fly's RTMP option streams what it shows. The same path is documented for the Neo with goggles.

head: Link from goggles to phone
Good for streaming?
Notes
rows: Stable, and the phone's Wi-Fi stays free to reach the computer.
The share uses wireless itself and can interfere; prefer the cable.

blocks.note: We have seen this path documented for DJI Goggles 3. With other goggles, check whether DJI Fly on the phone shows the live view and offers RTMP.

sections.h2: Set up the Avata 2 live stream

steps.t: Cable the goggles to the phone
steps.d: Connect the USB-C port of DJI Goggles 3 to the phone with an OTG-capable cable and open DJI Fly; tap GO FLY and confirm the live view appears.

steps.t: Join phone and computer to one network
steps.d: Connect the phone's Wi-Fi and the computer to the same Wi-Fi, or to a travel router or another phone's hotspot in the field.
Install DJI Live Bridge on a Mac or Windows PC and note the address it shows, like rtmp://192.168.1.20:1935/drone.
GO FLY → ••• → Transmission → Live Streaming Platforms → RTMP, enter the address and start. The preview appears in DJI Live Bridge.
Add Instagram, TikTok, YouTube or any RTMP server, choose vertical or horizontal, and press START LIVE before take-off.

blocks.alt: The Go live tab of DJI Live Bridge with the RTMP address for DJI Fly, the destinations and the START LIVE button.

blocks.note: The general DJI Fly settings, networks and firewall prompts are covered in the DJI Fly RTMP guide.

list: Start the stream before take-off. Once the goggles are on, you cannot see the computer; check the preview and the destinations first.
Let someone else watch the stream. A spotter can follow the destination cards and end the broadcast if needed.
Vertical FPV. Whole picture keeps the full horizon with a blurred fill — usually better for FPV than Fill screen, which crops the sides.
Android phones stream at a higher bitrate. DJI lists 5 or 3 Mbps on Android and 2 or 1 Mbps on iOS — fast FPV motion needs every bit.
No live view in DJI Fly: try another USB-C cable; it must carry data, not only power.
DJI Fly cannot connect to the computer: the phone's Wi-Fi is on another network, or the computer has a new address. Copy the address again.
The picture stutters: use the cable instead of the wireless share, and keep the phone close to the router.
Instagram rejects the stream: each Instagram key works once; create a new live video and update the key.

faq.q: Can the DJI Avata 2 live stream?
faq.a: Yes. DJI Goggles 3 share the live view with DJI Fly on a phone, and DJI Fly streams it over RTMP to DJI Live Bridge, which sends it to your platforms.

faq.q: Do I need a cable between the goggles and the phone?
faq.a: Goggles 3 can also share wirelessly, but the cable is more reliable and keeps the phone's Wi-Fi free to reach the computer.

faq.q: Can I stream the Avata 2 to Instagram or TikTok?
faq.a: Yes, through DJI Live Bridge. It turns the landscape FPV picture into vertical 1080×1920 and reaches Instagram over RTMPS, which DJI Fly cannot do itself.

faq.q: Who should run the stream while I fly?
faq.a: Start it before take-off and, if you can, let a spotter watch the computer. The pilot has the goggles on and cannot see the destination cards.
